questions.stem: All the new students were given one minute to _____ introduce themselves to the whole class.

If you _____ a traffic law, such as drinking and driving, you may not drive for some time.
Applying to college means sending in applications, writing study plans, and so on. It’s a long _____, and it makes students nervous.
Dr. Chu’s speech on the new energy source attracted great _____ from the audience at the conference.
Everyone in the office must attend the meeting tomorrow. There are no _____ allowed.
To make fresh lemonade, cut the lemon in half, _____ the juice into a bowl, and then add as much water and sugar as you like.

groups.passage: When it comes to Egypt, people think of pyramids and mummies, both of which are closely related to Egyptian religious beliefs. The ancient Egyptians believed firmly in life [[16]] death. When a person died, his or her soul was thought to travel to an underworld, where it [[17]] a series of judgments before it could progress to a better life in the next world. For the soul to travel smoothly, the body had to [[18]] unharmed. Thus, they learned how to preserve the body by drying it out, oiling and then [[19]] the body in linen, before placing it in the coffin. Egyptians also built pyramids as [[20]] for their kings, or pharaohs. The pyramid housed the pharaoh’s body together with priceless treasure, which would accompany him into the next world.

groups.passage:
Which is more valuable? Water or diamonds? Water is more useful to mankind than diamonds, and yet [[26]] are costlier. Why? Called the diamond-water paradox, this is a classic problem posed to students of economics.
The answer has to do with supply and demand. Being a rare natural resource, diamonds are [[27]] in supply. However, their demand is high because many people buy them to tell the world that they have money, [[28]] as conspicuous consumption in economics. In other words, the scarcity of goods is [[29]] causes humans to attribute value. If we [[30]] surrounded by an unending abundance of diamonds, we probably wouldn’t value them very much. Hence, diamonds carry a higher monetary value than water, even though we find more use for water.

tags.topic: the diamond-water paradox: scarcity, supply and demand

sections.instructions: 說明：第31題至第40題，每題一個空格，請依文意在文章後所提供的 (A) 到 (J) 選項中分別選出最適當者，並將其英文字母代號畫記在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。各題答對得1分；未作答、答錯、或畫記多於一個選項者，該題以零分計算。

groups.passage:
Popcorn is one of the snacks that rarely fail to make watching a movie more fun. However, the modern way of preparing this [[31]] snack may carry an unhappy secret. Research by the U.S. government now reports that microwave popcorn may contain substances that can cause health [[32]].
Researchers found that commercial popcorn companies often coat their microwave popcorn bags with a [[33]] called perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) which has been found to cause both cancer and lung disease in laboratory animals. Making matters worse, the artificial butter substitute that generally [[34]] with microwavable popcorn contains a common food-flavoring substance. This substance, according to health scientists, is [[35]] for some serious lung diseases.
For an easy and [[36]] alternative, nutritionists suggest that we pop our own popcorn. All that is [[37]] is a large, high pot, about four tablespoons of vegetable oil and a small handful of organic popcorn kernels. When the kernels start [[38]], shake the pot to let the steam escape and to let the unpopped kernels fall to the bottom. As soon as the popping slows down, [[39]] the pot from the stove. Then pour the popcorn into a bowl and season with a small [[40]] of real butter or olive oil and natural salt. And the healthy and fun snack is ready to serve.

sections.instructions: 說明︰第41題至第56題，每題4個選項，請分別根據各篇文章之文意選出最適當的一個答案，畫記在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。各題答對得2分；未作答、答錯、或畫記多於一個選項者，該題以零分計算。

groups.passage:
There is a long-held belief that when meeting someone, the more eye contact we have with the person, the better. The result is an unfortunate tendency for people making initial contact—in a job interview, for example—to stare fixedly at the other individual. However, this behavior is likely to make the interviewer feel very uncomfortable. Most of us are comfortable with eye contact lasting a few seconds. But eye contact which persists longer than that can make us nervous.
Another widely accepted belief is that powerful people in a society—often men—show their dominance over others by touching them in a variety of ways. In fact, research shows that in almost all cases, lower-status people initiate touch. Women also initiate touch more often than men do.
The belief that rapid speech and lying go together is also widespread and enduring. We react strongly—and suspiciously—to fast talk. However, the opposite is a greater cause for suspicion. Speech that is slow, because it is laced with pauses or errors, is a more reliable indicator of lying than the opposite.

groups.passage:
It is easy for us to tell our friends from our enemies. But can other animals do the same? Elephants can! They can use their sense of vision and smell to tell the difference between people who pose a threat and those who do not.
In Kenya, researchers found that elephants react differently to clothing worn by men of the Maasai and Kamba ethnic groups. Young Maasai men spear animals and thus pose a threat to elephants; Kamba men are mainly farmers and are not a danger to elephants.
In an experiment conducted by animal scientists, elephants were first presented with clean clothing or clothing that had been worn for five days by either a Maasai or a Kamba man. When the elephants detected the smell of clothing worn by a Maasai man, they moved away from the smell faster and took longer to relax than when they detected the smells of either clothing worn by Kamba men or clothing that had not been worn at all.
Garment color also plays a role, though in a different way. In the same study, when the elephants saw red clothing not worn before, they reacted angrily, as red is typically worn by Maasai men. Rather than running away as they did with the smell, the elephants acted aggressively toward the red clothing.
The researchers believe that the elephants’ emotional reactions are due to their different interpretations of the smells and the sights. Smelling a potential danger means that a threat is nearby and the best thing to do is run away and hide. Seeing a potential threat without its smell means that risk is low. Therefore, instead of showing fear and running away, the elephants express their anger and become aggressive.

questions.stem: According to the passage, which of the following statements is true about Kamba and Maasai people?

options.A: Maasai people are a threat to elephants.
options.B: Kamba people raise elephants for farming.
options.C: Both Kamba and Maasai people are elephant hunters.
options.D: Both Kamba and Maasai people traditionally wear red clothing.

questions.stem: How did the elephants react to smell in the study?

options.A: They attacked a man with the smell of new clothing.
options.B: They needed time to relax when smelling something unfamiliar.
options.C: They became anxious when they smelled Kamba-scented clothing.
options.D: They were frightened and ran away when they smelled their enemies.

questions.stem: What is the main idea of this passage?

options.A: Elephants use sight and smell to detect danger.
options.B: Elephants attack people who wear red clothing.
options.C: Scientists are now able to control elephants’ emotions.
options.D: Some Kenyan tribes understand elephants’ emotions very well.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about the elephant’s behavior from this passage?

options.B: Elephants have sharper sense of smell than sight.
options.C: Elephants are more intelligent than other animals.
options.D: Elephants tend to attack rather than escape when in danger.

tags.topic: elephants telling friends from enemies (Maasai vs. Kamba) by smell and clothing color

groups.passage:
It was something she had dreamed of since she was five. Finally, after years of training and intensive workouts, Deborah Duffey was going to compete in her first high school basketball game. The goals of becoming an outstanding player and playing college ball were never far from Deborah’s mind.
The game was against Mills High School. With 1:42 minutes left in the game, Deborah’s team led by one point. A player of Mills had possession of the ball, and Deborah ran to guard against her. As Deborah shuffled sideways to block the player, her knee went out and she collapsed on the court in burning pain. Just like that, Deborah’s season was over.
After suffering the bad injury, Deborah found that, for the first time in her life, she was in a situation beyond her control. Game after game, she could do nothing but sit on the sidelines watching others play the game that she loved so much.
Injuries limited Deborah’s time on the court as she hurt her knees three more times in the next five years. She had to spend countless hours in a physical therapy clinic to receive treatment. Her frequent visits there gave her a passion and respect for the profession. And Deborah began to see a new light in her life.
Currently a senior in college, Deborah focuses on pursuing a degree in physical therapy. After she graduates, Deborah plans to use her knowledge to educate people how to best take care of their bodies and cope with the feelings of hopelessness that she remembers so well.

questions.stem: What is the best title for this passage?
How did Deborah feel when she first hurt her knee?
What is true about Deborah Duffey?

options.A: She didn’t play on the court after the initial injury.
options.B: She injured her knee when she was trying to block her opponent.
options.C: She knew that she couldn’t be a basketball player when she was a child.
options.D: She refused to seek professional assistance to help her recover from her injuries.

questions.stem: What was the new light that Deborah saw in her life?

options.A: To help people take care of their bodies.
options.B: To become a teacher of Physical Education.
options.C: To become an outstanding basketball player.
options.D: To receive treatment in a physical therapy office.

tags.topic: a basketball player whose knee injuries led her to study physical therapy

groups.passage: Redwood trees are the tallest plants on the earth, reaching heights of up to 100 meters. They are also known for their longevity, typically 500 to 1000 years, but sometimes more than 2000 years. A hundred million years ago, in the age of dinosaurs, redwoods were common in the forests of a much more moist and tropical North America. As the climate became drier and colder, they retreated to a narrow strip along the Pacific coast of Northern California. The trunk of redwood trees is very stout and usually forms a single straight column. It is covered with a beautiful soft, spongy bark. This bark can be pretty thick, well over two feet in the more mature trees. It gives the older trees a certain kind of protection from insects, but the main benefit is that it keeps the center of the tree intact from moderate forest fires because of its thickness. This fire resistant quality explains why the giant redwood grows to live that long. While most other types of trees are destroyed by forest fires, the giant redwood actually prospers because of them. Moderate fires will clear the ground of competing plant life, and the rising heat dries and opens the ripe cones of the redwood, releasing many thousands of seeds onto the ground below. New trees are often produced from sprouts, little baby trees, which form at the base of the trunk. These sprouts grow slowly, nourished by the root system of the “mother” tree. When the main tree dies, the sprouts are then free to grow as full trees, forming a “fairy ring” of trees around the initial tree. These trees, in turn, may give rise to more sprouts, and the cycle continues.

questions.stem: Why were redwood trees more prominent in the forests of North America millions of years ago?

options.A: The trees were taller and stronger.
options.B: The soil was softer for seeds to sprout.
options.C: The climate was warmer and more humid.
options.D: The temperature was lower along the Pacific coast.

questions.stem: What does a “fairy ring” in the last paragraph refer to?

refers_to.note: 原卷粗體（選文最後一段 forming a “fairy ring” of trees）；Word 版該 run 為粗體

options.C: Insect holes around an old tree.
options.D: Young trees surrounding a mature tree.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a function of the tree bark as mentioned in the passage?

options.A: It allows redwood trees to bear seeds.
options.B: It prevents redwood trees from attack by insects.
options.C: It helps redwood trees absorb moisture in the air.
options.D: It makes redwood trees more beautiful and appealing.

questions.stem: Why do redwood trees grow to live that long according to the passage?

options.A: They have heavy and straight tree trunks.
options.B: They are properly watered and nourished.
options.C: They are more resistant to fire damage than other trees.
options.D: They produce many young trees to sustain their life cycle.

tags.topic: redwood trees: longevity, fire-resistant bark and fairy rings

（一）中譯英，為文意相連貫的兩個小題，每小題4分，共8分；依各句所呈現的句法與詞彙進行評分。
本題型旨在評量考試是否能將中文句子譯成正確、通順、達意的英文句子之能力。今年中譯英的句型與詞彙，皆為高中生應該熟習的，評量的重點在於考生是否能運用熟悉的字詞（例如：夜市night markets、在地文化local culture、吸引attract、成千上萬hundreds and thousands of、觀光客tourists或visitors等）與基本句型（例如：have long been regarded as等的用法），將中文句子翻譯成正確且達意的英文句子。所測驗之標的詞彙（target words）都屬於大考中心參考詞彙表四級內之詞彙，中等程度以上的考生如果能夠使用正確的句型與字詞，並且注意拼字，應該能有理想的表現。和往年一樣，今年的考生在拼字（如：將night markets寫成nightmarkets，或者把culture寫成colture等）、單複數（countries寫成countrys）的掌握仍有進步的空間。試題之參考答案及評分標準，請見以下說明1：

questions.stem: 提示︰請仔細觀察以下三幅連環圖片的內容，並想像第四幅圖片可能的發展，寫出一個涵蓋連環圖片內容並有完整結局的故事。
questions.scoring_notes:
（二）英文作文則採看圖作文的題型，以連環漫畫的形式呈現，但第四張圖片空白，讓考生發揮想像力，自由發展；考生必須根據提示，運用所學詞彙、句法寫出切合主題、並具有統一性與連貫性的短文，占分比例與往年一樣，總分為20分。
評分標準：
本大題總分20分。今年的英文作文與去年的看圖作文相同，四格圖片只畫了三格，並沒有提供結局，希望給考生更多的寫作發揮空間。英文作文主要在於評量考生能否具備基礎的語法能力及使用適當詞彙、句型以寫出一篇具連貫性、統一性的英文作文。目前，英文作文採整體式評分（holistic scoring），分為五等級：特優（19-20分）、優（15-18分）、可（10-14分）、差（5-9分）、劣（0-4分）。評分主要依據為考生的作答內容，閱卷委員仔細評估其內容是否切題、組織是否具連貫性、句子結構與用字是否能妥適表達文意，以及拼字與標點符號是否使用正確等。但為確認評分之一致性，在試閱時，閱卷委員皆被要求須完全理解各分項的評分標準，英文作文的分項式評分指標包含下列5項：內容（5分）、組織（5分）、文法句構（4分）、字彙拼字（4分），及體例（2分）（詳見表1）。根據作答說明，文長約100至120個字詞，若字數嚴重不足，則扣1分。
表1：英文作文分項式評分指標2（等級：優／可／差／劣）
內容｜優：主題(句)清楚切題，並有具體、完整的相關細節支持。(5-4分)｜可：主題不夠清楚或突顯，部分相關敘述發展不全。(3分)｜差：主題不明，大部分相關敘述發展不全或與主題無關。(2-1分)｜劣：文不對題或沒寫(凡文不對題或沒寫者，其他各項均以零分計算)。(0分)
組織｜優：重點分明，有開頭、發展、結尾，前後連貫，轉承語使用得當。(5-4分)｜可：重點安排不妥，前後發展比例與轉承語使用欠妥。(3分)｜差：重點不明、前後不連貫。(2-1分)｜劣：全文毫無組織或未按提示寫作。(0分)
文法、句構｜優：全文幾無文法錯誤，文句結構富變化。(4分)｜可：文法錯誤少，且未影響文意之表達。(3分)｜差：文法錯誤多，且明顯影響文意之表達。(2-1分)｜劣：全文文法錯誤嚴重，導致文意不明。(0分)
字彙、拼字｜優：用字精確、得宜，且幾無拼字錯誤。(4分)｜可：字詞單調、重複，用字偶有不當，少許拼字錯誤，但不影響文意之表達。(3分)｜差：用字、拼字錯誤多，明顯影響文意之表達。(2-1分)｜劣：只寫出或抄襲與題意有關的零碎字詞。(0分)
體例｜優、可（合併一格）：格式、標點、大小寫幾無錯誤。(2分)｜差：格式、標點、大小寫等有錯誤，但不影響文意之表達。(1分)｜劣：違背基本的寫作體例或格式，標點、大小寫等錯誤甚多。(0分)
2.改編自張武昌等（民93）「英文寫作能力測驗規劃研究（VI）」研究報告。台北：大考中心。後經「95學年度學科能力測驗人工閱卷英文考科評分標準訂定會議」修改。

extraction.method: 題本文字以 Word 版 paper-2.doc 為主（soffice --headless 轉成 docx 後，以 lxml 走訪 document.xml 的全部 w:r：底線 run 內的數字轉成 [[題號]]，第13題的底線空白轉成 _____），再以程式將全部 270 個文字欄位（大題標題、部分標題、說明、題組標示、選文各段、題幹、選項、選項庫）與 pdftotext -layout（paper-1.pdf）逐段比對（英文比對連續詞序列、中文去空白後比對子字串），並反向核對 PDF 英文詞頻與 JSON 一致；差異只有三處版面造成的非文字差異（見 issues）。以 Read 看 PDF 全部 8 頁頁面影像確認段落切分、粗體、斜體與底線；英文作文四格圖改用 Word 內嵌的 3489×2524 原圖逐格裁切放大判讀描述。答案取自 answer.pdf（pdftotext -layout）。評分原則取自 scoring.pdf（選才電子報第199期〈100年學科能力測驗英文考科非選擇題評分說明〉，網頁列印 PDF，正文與左側欄位交錯，依頁面影像重排）逐字摘錄；中譯英參考答案是第2–3頁的大括弧樹狀圖片（pdftotext 抓不到），以 pdfimages 取出原始圖檔（2224×1358、2359×1019）人工轉錄。統計以 xlrd 讀 stats-1.xls（英文工作表：答對率 P、高分組 Ph、低分組 Pl、鑑別度 D）、stats-2.xls（英文工作表：選項分析 T／H／L 列、未答）、stats-3.xls（英文科非選擇題分數人數統計表），並以程式交叉核對（選項分析標 * 的選項＝官方答案；T 列正答比例＝P；H／L 列正答比例＝Ph／Pl（一處差 1 個百分點，見 issues）；D＝Ph−Pl；非選擇題各分數段人數加總＝到考人數）。 查證（verifier）：另以獨立程式重新核對——56 題答案逐題對照 answer.pdf 文字層並以 Read 看頁面影像確認，全部一致；56 題題幹、全部 184 個選項（各題 (A)–(D) 依序連續比對）、8 篇選文各段（[[題號]] 還原成題號後）與 10 個選項庫字詞，以去除多餘空白後的逐字元子字串比對 pdftotext -layout 結果，並另以自行轉檔的 Word 版逐字比對，除第13題空格（PDF 為畫線、Word 為底線空白）外完全一致；PDF 與 JSON 的英文 token 多重集合比對，差異只剩選項代號與封面「2B」；各篇選文字數（131／146／126／217／175／289／262／287，文意選填 PDF 多 2 是空格與標點分開）、段落數（1／2／2／3／3／5／5／3）、首末句皆與 PDF 一致；大題標題、部分標題、說明、題組標示、中譯英題目與作文提示（去空白後）全部與 PDF 文字層一致；Read 看題本 8 頁影像確認粗體／斜體／底線與段落切分；中譯英參考答案以 pdfimages 重新取出兩張分歧圖逐項核對 accepted_answers 與 4 段虛線切分；評分說明各段落與表1 二十個儲存格依 scoring.pdf 頁面影像與 pdftotext 逐格核對；作文四格圖以 Word 內嵌原圖裁切放大核對描述；統計以 xlrd 重讀三個 xls，56 題 P／Ph／Pl／D、T／H／L 各選項比例、未答比例（僅第56題 T 列 1%；L 列第45、55、56題 1%）與兩題非選擇題各分數段人數／百分比全部比對一致。標註逐題複核 answer_pos、test_point、item_type，未發現明顯錯誤，未修改。
issues: 結構核對：與 gsat-spec.json legacy_gsat 期別「94–110」一致——詞彙 1–15（15分）、綜合測驗 16–30（3篇×5題，15分）、文意選填 31–40（A–J，10分）、閱讀測驗 41–56（4篇×4題，每題2分，32分）、中譯英 2題×4分、英文作文 20分；第壹部分單選題 72分＋第貳部分非選擇題 28分＝100分；封面「考試時間：100 分鐘」「單選題共 56 題」「非選擇題共 2 大題」。第一大題標題為「詞彙」（spec：102 起才改稱「詞彙題」），非選擇題第一大題為「中譯英」、選擇題說明為「未作答、答錯、或畫記多於一個選項者，該題以零分計算」，皆與 spec changes「100」相符；作文「文長約100至120個單詞（words）」與 essay_length_by_year「100」相符。本年綜合測驗三篇沒有題組標示（spec 記載 103 起才有），閱讀測驗的題組標示寫法是「41-44 為題組」（不是後來的「第41至44題為題組」），照錄於 group_label。無差異。
validator warning「題號重複 [1, 2]」為預期：中譯英兩題題本編為 1.、2.，英文作文沒有題號（no 填 1）；no 必須是整數，故沿用題本編號，並以 label「中譯英1」「中譯英2」「作文」區分，label 無重複（與 gsat-102～108 做法相同）。

中譯英參考答案：scoring.pdf「參考答案：第1題」「參考答案：第2題」是大括弧樹狀圖片，以 pdfimages 取出原圖人工轉錄為 accepted_answers：{a|b} 表示同一個大括弧內擇一，( ) 照原圖表示可省略（依 scoring.pdf 註1「{ }（大括弧）表示皆為可使用之字詞，而（ ）則表示可省略之字詞」）。第1題原圖主詞（Taiwan’s night markets／Night markets in Taiwan／The night markets in Taiwan）在上一列，下一列以一個大括弧分成兩組述語：have ({long/already}) been {regarded/recognized/considered/known/thought of} {as representing/as a (good) symbol of} {our/the} local culture.，以及 have ({long/already}) been {considered/known/thought/recognized} to {(well)/(be able to)} represent {our/the} local culture.；因此 accepted_answers 第1題分兩條，各自接上主詞的大括弧。第二組的「(well)」「(be able to)」在原圖是同一個大括弧內的兩個可省略項，照錄為 {(well)|(be able to)}，即 to represent／to well represent／to be able to represent 皆可。第2題：{Every/Each} year {they/the (night) markets} attract {hundreds and thousands of/thousands and thousands of/hundreds and hundreds of/hundreds of thousands of/millions of/thousands of} {tourists/visitors} (coming) from {(many) different/many} {countries./nations.}。answer 取各大括弧第一個選項組成的句子（不含可省略字詞），不是官方另列的整句；官方沒有另外提供完整參考句。原圖以虛線把每題切成 4 個計分部分（第1題：主詞｜have long been regarded｜as representing｜our local culture；第2題：Every year｜they attract｜hundreds and thousands of tourists｜(coming) from different countries），對應評分標準「2.各部分獨立且各為1分」；此分段未另設欄位，只記於此。（v1.1 修正與結構化）以 pdfimages 原圖放大重看：兩組述語中 long／already 外框都是左右對稱、沒有中間尖角的大圓括號，與其他位置的大括號（有中間尖角）不同，依註1「（ ）表示可省略之字詞」改記為 ({long|already})，即 have long been／have already been／have been 皆可（原記為大括號擇一）。兩題改以 answer_segments 表示，answer_is_composite: true（官方沒有整句）。第1題兩組述語的動詞與後接結構相依（regarded／thought of 只接 as…，thought 只接 to…），所以把「動詞＋as…／to…」攤平成一段 27 種寫法（5×3＋4×3），主詞、({long|already})、{our|the} 各為一段；第2題沒有相依，(night)、(coming)、(many) 以空字串表示可省略。

中譯英 scoring_notes：兩題共用同一段文字（原文同時說明兩句，無法逐句切開），依序為 scoring.pdf 開頭段落中的「（一）中譯英，為文意相連貫的兩個小題…依各句所呈現的句法與詞彙進行評分。」、中譯英說明整段（含「請見以下說明1：」的註腳編號 1）、「評分標準：」1–4 點，以及頁尾註「1.{ }（大括弧）表示皆為可使用之字詞，而（ ）則表示可省略之字詞。」，以換行分隔。原文「本題型旨在評量考試是否能…」的「考試」（應為考生）照錄未改（頁面影像確認）；pdftotext 在「熟悉的字詞（例如：夜市night markets…成千上萬」一行因左右對齊在每個字之間插入空白，已依頁面影像去除。scoring.pdf 中關於閱卷流程（143位閱卷委員、評分標準訂定會議、螢幕閱卷、一二閱差距超過「中譯英部分差距大於2分，英文作文部分差距大於5分」時由第三閱評分、新增第四閱）的段落與題目內容無關，未收錄。

英文作文 scoring_notes：依序為 scoring.pdf 開頭段落中的「（二）英文作文則採看圖作文的題型…總分為20分。」、作文「評分標準：」整段、「表1：英文作文分項式評分指標2」與頁尾註2（表名後的 2 是註腳編號）。表1 依 gsat-102 的寫法線性化成「項目｜優：…(分數)｜可：…｜差：…｜劣：…」，表頭的「（等級：優／可／差／劣）」與體例列的「優、可（合併一格）」是為了說明原表結構而加的文字，其餘逐字；文法句構「優」欄原文字層為「全文幾無文法錯誤， 文句結構富變化。」，逗號後的空白是網頁排版殘留，已去除。原文不一致處照錄：評分標準寫「文長約100至120個字詞」（題本為「單詞（words）」）；scoring.pdf 重抄的作文說明作「2. 文長約為100至120個單詞 (words)。」，與題本「2.文長約100至120個單詞（words）。」不同，instructions 以題本為準。本年作文評分為五項（含體例2分），與 spec 所記 106 年起才改為四項一致。官方沒有範文，answer 為 null。
英文作文圖（s6g1 figures）：四格連環圖只以圖片呈現，題本文字層與 Word 版都沒有圖中文字；依 Word 內嵌原圖逐格描述，圖中唯一的文字「化妝舞會」（第1格招牌）逐字抄錄，caption 用圖框角落圓圈內的編號 1–4。第3格窗內三人的表情依線條判讀（中間捲髮男子張嘴怒吼並指向樓下、嘴邊有叫罵符號；下方男子皺眉；左上角男子旁有多個問號），圖中沒有出現第1、2格的女孩。
英文作文 tags：題目要求依三幅連環圖片並想像第四幅（問號空白格）寫出有完整結局的故事，essay_type 標 picture；題目沒有規定段數，不填 paragraphs；word_requirement 依說明「文長約100至120個單詞」標 about 100 to 120 words。

選擇題統計：stats-1.xls 與 stats-2.xls 交叉核對——選項分析中標 * 的選項＝官方答案（56 題全部）；T 列正答比例＝P（56 題全部）；H 列正答比例＝Ph（56 題全部）；L 列正答比例＝Pl，只有第37題不同（L 列正答 G 為 18%，stats-1 的 Pl 為 17%，兩表各自四捨五入），low_group 取 stats-1、option_rates_low 取 stats-2，照原表保留；D＝Ph−Pl 全部 56 題成立。各題 option_rates（加未答）因四捨五入加總為 0.99–1.01。
選擇題統計：除 schema 欄位外，另存 option_rates_high／option_rates_low（stats-2.xls 選項分析的高分組 H、低分組 L 列）與 omit_rate（全體未答比例，T 列；本年只有第56題 T 列未答 1%，其餘 0；L 列另有第45、55、56題未答 1%，未另存欄位）；stats-1.xls 的五組通過率 Pa–Pe 與 D1–D4 未收錄。

非選擇題統計：stats-3.xls 只有「第一題（中譯英，滿分8分，兩小題合計）」與「第二題（英文作文，滿分20分）」的分數人數分布，無法拆到中譯英各小題，因此放在 sections[s5].stats 與 sections[s6].stats 的 score_distribution（schema 未定義此欄位，沿用 gsat-102 等檔的做法），小題層級 stats 為 null。rate 為原表百分比÷100，分母是報名人數 146,302（含缺考 2,450；到考 143,852，與 stats-1.xls 表頭一致）；已核對兩題各分數段人數加總＝到考人數 143,852。原表分數區間「9.00- 9.99」等的空白已去除；第一題 9 分以上的列在原表為空白，未收錄。
